text.da: Guten Tag, ich bin der Vater von Lea.
Jetzt sind wir in der Stadt.
text.en: Now we are in the city.

text.da: Nächste Woche fahre ich wieder nach Flensburg.
text.en: Next week I'm going to Flensburg again.

text.da: Das Zimmer ist ein bisschen klein.
text.en: The room is a bit small.
Do you have any money left?

text.da: Das Jahr ist schon fast vorbei.
text.en: The year is almost over already.
There are a lot of people here.

text.da: Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?
text.en: How do you say that in German?

text.da: Das ist alles neu für mich.
Die Reise ist lang, aber schön.
text.en: The trip is long but lovely.

text.da: Das ist der letzte Bus heute.
text.en: That is the last bus today.

text.da: Mein Partner und ich wohnen hier.
text.en: My partner and I live here.

text.da: Kann ich hier das WLAN benutzen?
text.en: Can I use the Wi-Fi here?
Excuse me, is anyone sitting here?
I would like to see the world.

text.da: Wir sind in der gleichen Klasse.
text.en: We are in the same class.
The way is here on the left.
How much is that in kroner?

text.da: Ist hier noch ein Platz frei?
text.en: Is there still a free seat here?
Would you like to try that?
Excuse me, what is your name?

text.da: Das ist der Grund, warum ich hier bin.
text.en: That's the reason why I'm here.

text.da: Auf diese Weise geht es schneller.
Der Bus kommt in einer Stunde.
text.en: The bus comes in an hour.
Do you already know the story?

text.da: Ich bin seit einem Monat hier.
text.en: I've been here for a month.

text.da: Ich spreche die Sprache ein bisschen.
text.en: I speak the language a little.

text.da: Kannst du mir ein Beispiel geben?
text.en: Can you give me an example?

text.da: Wir treffen uns um halb drei.
text.en: We're meeting at half past two.

about.usageEn: An everyday greeting for any time of day. On the phone it is also how you answer.
The polite greeting from late morning to early evening, for shops, offices and people you do not know.
Asks about a person. The verb comes straight after it: wer ist …?, wer kommt …?
Says something has happened earlier than expected. In a question it means yet: Bist du schon da?

about.meaningEn: There is; there are. Gibt es …? is: is there …?
about.usageEn: Says that something exists or is available. It stays es gibt for one thing or many.
Greets someone arriving. Add in with a place: Willkommen in Flensburg!
The everyday thanks. Danke für … names the thing; danke schön is a little warmer.
Noch ein … asks for one more. With a verb it means still: Ich bin noch hier.
Points at a place near the speaker or the listener. Ist … da? asks whether someone is in.
After a verb it says you like doing it: Ich lese gern. On its own it answers a thank-you or a request.
The ordinary yes. Ja, gern is a friendly yes, please.
Says something happens at this moment. It often stands first for emphasis.
The place where the speaker is. Hier ist … hands something over or points at it.
This day. It can stand first or later in the sentence.
Something happens another time. Noch einmal asks for a repeat; wieder describes one.
Makes an adjective stronger: sehr gut. Danke sehr is a polite thanks.
Softens what follows. Ein bisschen Deutsch is a little German.
Asks about manner or state. In Wie heißt du? and Wie alt …? English says what or how.
Adds the same to something already said. Ich auch is: me too.
Asks about time. The verb follows it: Wann kommt …?
Several people doing one thing. In a café, zusammen asks for one bill.
Asks about a thing. Was ist das? is the first question of any new place.
Says something belongs to you. It is mein before a der or das noun and meine before a die noun.
The friendly goodbye. Auf Wiedersehen is the polite one.
All of it at once. Alles gut? asks whether everything is fine.
The day after today. Small letter; Morgen with a capital is the morning.
Makes a request polite. After a thank-you it means you are welcome; wie bitte? asks for a repeat.
Joins two ideas that pull apart. In Das ist aber … it adds surprise.
Says no to a verb, an adjective or a whole sentence. A noun takes kein instead.
Asks you to choose. Its ending follows the noun: welcher Bus, welche Tür, welches Haus.

example.en: Which bus goes to the station?

about.usageEn: Joins two words or two sentences. Und du? passes a question back.
The ordinary no. Nein, danke declines politely.
Kann ich …? and Kannst du …? ask for permission or help. The other verb goes to the end.
Not anything. Das macht nichts is: never mind, no problem.
Makes a word stronger or asks whether something is true: Wirklich?
Asks about a place. Wo ist …? is the question for finding anything.
Says where someone or something comes from: Ich komme aus Kanada.
Opens a question to a stranger, or apologises for a small thing.

example.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

about.usageEn: Agrees or says something is fine. German uses it just as English does.
Points at a manner. So ist das is: that is how it is.
The polite way to ask for or offer something: Ich möchte …, Möchtest du …?

example.en: I would like a bread roll.

about.usageEn: Bis + a time is a goodbye: bis morgen, bis bald, bis dann.
The speaker and others. The verb ends in -en: wir sind, wir gehen.
Speaks to one person you know well, a child or someone your own age. Strangers and officials get Sie.
Before an adjective it means too much: zu groß, zu teuer.
Me after a verb or word that takes the dative: mir ist kalt, gib mir, hilf mir.
The du-form when you are the one something happens to: Ich sehe dich.
Wie viel asks about an amount, wie viele about things you can count.
Asks for a reason. The answer often starts with weil.
Points at something near. Its ending follows the noun: dieser Bus, diese Tür, dieses Haus.
Says no to a noun: kein Geld, keine Zeit. Other words take nicht.
A place or a span of time: in Flensburg, in einer Stunde.
Um + a time: um acht, um halb drei.
Says how long something has been true. German uses the present tense with it.

example.en: I have been learning German since Monday.

about.usageEn: Leaves something out: ohne Zucker, ohne mich.
The past of ist: das war gut, es war schön.
Opposes something, or gives a rough time: gegen acht.

example.en: I will come at about eight.

about.usageEn: Asks about origin. The answer uses aus: Ich komme aus …

example.en: Where is the train coming from?
